disclaimer: Built from widely shared W211/OM646 owner and workshop knowledge, adjusted for hot, dusty driving (Tunisia). Not an official Mercedes document. Always confirm with a mechanic, and follow your service booklet where it differs.

intervals.why: Engine oil + filter. 10,000 km is on the safe side for heat, dust and short trips. Use a diesel oil meeting MB 229.3 or 229.5.
Dusty roads clog it faster than the book says. A clogged filter costs power and fuel.
Diesel quality varies. The fuel filter protects the expensive common-rail injectors.
Pollen/dust filter for the cabin air and A/C.
Pads wear with use, not time. This is an inspection reminder: check thickness and replace when worn.
Brake fluid absorbs water over time and boils sooner. Change every 2 years whatever the mileage. Safety item.

how: Engine off, car on flat ground, engine cold.
Open the bonnet. Find the small plastic tank with a brake symbol on the cap, at the back of the engine bay near the windscreen (it can sit under a plastic cover).
Look at the level through the side of the tank: it should sit between MIN and MAX.
Look at the colour of the fluid. Don't open the cap unless you have to: brake fluid damages paint.
check.fine: Clear to light yellow, level between MIN and MAX.
check.old: Amber or darker yellow, like weak tea. Still works, but it's absorbing water. Plan a change.
check.bad: Dark brown or black, or the level is below MIN. A low level can mean worn pads or a leak: see a mechanic soon.

intervals.why: Old coolant corrodes the cooling system. Use the correct MB-approved coolant.

how: Only check with the engine COLD. Never open the cap on a hot engine: it can spray boiling coolant.
Open the bonnet. Find the see-through plastic tank with a temperature or coolant symbol on the cap.
Check the level on the side of the tank: between MIN and MAX.
Look at the colour and the inside of the tank.
check.fine: Clean, bright colour (blue, green or pink depending on the type), level between MIN and MAX.
check.old: Faded or a bit murky. Plan a change.
check.bad: Brown, rusty, oily film on top, or you keep having to top it up. That can mean a leak or worse: see a mechanic.

intervals.why: Manual gearbox oil is often called lifetime, but at high mileage a change keeps shifts smooth.
Worn glow plugs make cold starts hard. Inspect around this mileage.

how: Do this on a cold morning, after the car sat all night (from midnightblue: cold starts tell you everything).
Turn the key to the second position without starting. The yellow coil light comes on: that's the glow plugs heating up.
Wait until the coil light goes out, then start.
Notice three things: how long you crank, how the engine sounds in the first seconds, and how much white smoke comes out.
check.fine: Starts on the first try once the coil light is off, runs smoothly within a few seconds, little or no white smoke.
check.old: Needs longer cranking on cold mornings, shakes or runs rough for the first seconds, a puff of white smoke that clears fast. One or two plugs may be weak.
check.bad: Hard or no start when cold, lots of white smoke, misfiring until warm, or the coil light flashing or staying on while driving (a glow system fault). A mechanic can test each plug. Removal on high-mileage diesels needs care: old plugs can seize.

issues.name: Injector seal leak ("black death")
symptoms: ticking or puffing sound from the engine top
diesel or exhaust smell in the cabin
black crusty deposits around the injectors
issues.check: Look under the engine cover around each injector for black tar-like crust. Fix early: once the carbon sets in, injectors get very hard to remove.

issues.name: Worn injectors
issues.check: A diesel specialist can run a leak-off (return flow) test to see which injector is worn.

issues.name: Turbocharger wear
symptoms: loud whistle or siren sound under load
issues.check: Check turbo shaft play and look for oil in the boost hoses. Let the engine idle 30 seconds before switching off after hard driving.

issues.name: EGR valve and intake sooting
issues.check: Read the fault codes, then have the EGR valve and intake cleaned. Short trips make it worse.

issues.name: Timing chain and tensioner
symptoms: rattle for a few seconds at cold start
issues.check: At high mileage, have a mechanic check chain stretch. Ignoring a stretched chain can destroy the engine.

issues.name: Worn engine and gearbox mounts
symptoms: clunk when pulling away or shifting
engine moving a lot when revved
issues.check: Watch the engine while someone revs it gently in gear with the handbrake on.

issues.name: SBC brake system (if fitted)
symptoms: pump noise from the brake unit
issues.check: Most W211s built until about 2006, including 2004 cars, have the electro-hydraulic SBC brakes. The SBC unit has a limited life. Ask a Mercedes specialist to read its status. Any SBC warning means see a mechanic before driving far.

issues.name: Thermostat stuck open
symptoms: engine takes very long to warm up
issues.check: If the gauge doesn't reach about 80°C after 10-15 minutes of driving, the thermostat is likely stuck.

issues.name: Glow plugs
symptoms: glow plug light stays on or flashes
issues.check: A mechanic can test each glow plug's resistance. Replace the whole set.

issues.name: Auxiliary belt and tensioner
symptoms: squeal at start or with A/C on
issues.check: Look at the belt for cracks and the tensioner for wobble with the engine running.

issues.name: Rust spots
symptoms: bubbling paint on door bottoms, wheel arches, boot lid
rust around jacking points and subframes
issues.check: Check underneath once a year, especially jacking points and subframe mounts. Treat small spots early.
